messages:
alvaro: Heads up — after the 1.26 upgrade the cluster-autoscaler stopped adding GPU nodegroups for prod-gpu workloads. Pods are pending with resource requests for nvidia.com/gpu and nothing scales up.

jess: ugh. did the node pool API change in the cloud provider? any errors in the autoscaler logs? :thinking_face: 

alvaro: logs show: 
```
I0524 15:12:34 main.go:210] Failed to find any node group for labels selector: 'node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=gpu-rtx'
E0524 15:12:34 scale_up.go:142] No candidates for scale up
```

maria: that selector is what our kube2cloud controller used to generate. We moved to the new nodegroup CRD in the upgrade — annotation key changed from cloud.redwood.io/node-group to cloud.redwood.io/nodegroup (no hyphen). Autoscaler config still references the old annotation.

alvaro: ahhh nice catch. So CA can't map pending pods to a nodegroup. That matches the logs.

ops-oncall: temporary mitigation — scaling our backup gpu-autoscale pool manually to 10 nodes. Will buy time while we patch. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

jess: can we hotfix the node selector in the autoscaler config? Where is it configured now? I thought we use the cloud provider discovery.

maria: discovery reads nodegroup labels from cloud-controller-manager which got bumped too. The controller now exposes label cloud.redwood.com/nodegroup-name. I'll open a quick PR to map both old/new keys for backward compat.

alvaro: paste the minimal patch you plan to apply — ops needs to decide whether to roll the autoscaler or revert the cluster upgrade.

maria: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/cluster-autoscaler/merge_requests/412 — basically add a fallback: if annotation cloud.redwood.io/node-group not found then try cloud.redwood.io/nodegroup and cloud.redwood.com/nodegroup-name. Patch also adds a unit test.

infra-bot: deploy-started autoscaler-canary -> infra-canary (image:ca:1.0.8-hotfix) by maria at 2026-03-18T15:45:12Z

jess: canary looks healthy on staging. I'm watching scale-up tests (gpu-pod job).

infra-bot: alert: 2 pending GPU pods in prod-gpu awaiting nodes (since 12m)

alvaro: after canary we applied to prod. Autoscaler now logs: 
```
I0524 16:02:07 discovery.go:98] Found nodegroup via cloud.redwood.com/nodegroup-name=prod-gpu-rtx
I0524 16:02:08 scale_up.go:54] Scale up triggered: +3 nodes for nodegroup prod-gpu-rtx (reason: unschedulable pods)
```

ops-oncall: verified pods transitioned from Pending -> Running, GPU allocation looks correct. Cost impact minimal since nodes were spin-up only for ~20 minutes for backlog.

jess: follow-up: add migration note to upgrade runbook, and schedule a sweep to remove old annotations after 2 weeks. Also add an e2e test to catch this mapping regression.

maria: will do. Filed tickets: INFRA-1024 (hotfix + canary), INFRA-1025 (runbook + e2e), INFRA-1026 (cleanup annotations).

alvaro: thanks everyone. Good outcome. Leaving the manual pool scaled to 2 until next maintenance window.

ops-oncall: thumbs up. Closing incident once cleanup tasks are done. :white_check_mark:
